groups.title: Repository identity, defaults and collaboration surfaces
groups.applicability: Every repository; preserve owner decisions about visibility, licensing and audience.

options.name: visibility / private
options.decision_rule: Preserve observed visibility; assess access and discoverability before a requested change, never make a private project public as routine setup.
options.verification: Re-read visibility and intended reader access; inspect fork implications before changing.

options.name: default_branch
options.decision_rule: Retain the current branch unless migration is required; discover branch names before configuring CI, templates or closing links.
options.verification: Read repository default_branch, ref SHA and PR bases after any authorized rename.

options.name: has_issues / has_projects / has_wiki / has_discussions
options.decision_rule: Enable the surfaces the project will actively use; enabling a repository Projects tab does not create or configure an owner Project.
options.verification: Read each flag and follow the actual tab and linked owner Project.

options.name: description / homepage / topics
options.decision_rule: Use concise purpose and a working primary documentation URL; preserve unrelated topics and owner-defined metadata.
options.verification: Read metadata and open rendered links; check topic replacement semantics before writing.

options.name: autolinks.key_prefix / url_template / is_alphanumeric
options.decision_rule: Add only for a real external tracker; choose a non-colliding prefix and correct numeric versus alphanumeric matching.
options.verification: Read rule IDs and test a harmless rendered example without sending a comment.

options.name: archived / disabled
options.decision_rule: Archive only when work truly ends; do not archive to represent a finished milestone or Project.
options.verification: Re-read flags, open work and expected read-only behavior; record unarchive recovery path.

pitfalls: Repository flag defaults vary with creation path and owner settings; never infer actual configuration from product availability.

groups.title: Source changes, history and repository derivation
groups.applicability: Every code repository; LFS/submodules/templates/forks only where present.

options.name: content.ref / expected sha
options.decision_rule: Read immutable refs for evidence; use Git for multi-file work and expected old SHAs for API writes.
options.verification: Inspect resulting commit tree and parents plus changed-file list; reconcile timeout before retry.

options.name: ref.force / git push strategy
options.decision_rule: Preserve human commits; default to non-force updates, compare remote head and use a lease only for authorized history rewrite.
options.verification: Fetch and compare old/new ref OIDs; stop if remote changed unexpectedly.

options.name: merge history
options.decision_rule: Follow repository policy; merge preserves branch commits, squash gives one logical commit, rebase rewrites commit identities.
options.verification: Match resulting base-branch commit and PR merge metadata; keep issue/PR links as decision history.

options.name: template.include_all_branches / fork.default_branch_only
options.decision_rule: Template copies start a separate history; forks preserve an upstream relationship. Choose based on contribution versus new-project intent.
options.verification: Inspect parent/source or is_template relationship and compare expected branches/files.

options.name: LFS / submodule checkout
options.decision_rule: Fetch only required objects and pinned submodules; never treat an LFS pointer or gitlink as tested source content.
options.verification: Verify actual object bytes, submodule OIDs and executable/symlink modes.

options.name: comment anchor
options.decision_rule: Commit comments discuss a specific historical revision; use a PR review thread for an actionable PR finding.
options.verification: Read returned comment ID, commit_id and line metadata; retain URL when following up.

pitfalls: A Git clone does not contain issues, review conversations, Project configuration or Wiki history. Separate evidence stores are needed for those records.

groups.title: Who receives review and when
groups.applicability: Repositories accepting PRs; stricter ownership only with available qualified reviewers.

options.name: CODEOWNERS location / matching order
options.decision_rule: Use one authoritative file on the PR base branch, broad ownership first and narrow overrides later; list multiple owners together.
options.verification: Read actual base-branch file, query CODEOWNERS errors and map representative changed paths.

options.name: owner eligibility
options.decision_rule: Reuse real maintainers; do not invent a reviewer or broaden team visibility/access to make routing work.
options.verification: Verify team visibility and repository role; inspect requests on a matching ready PR.

options.name: requested_reviewers / requested_teams
options.decision_rule: Request the smallest relevant set; requests notify people, so repository setup alone is not authority to send them.
options.verification: Read outstanding review requests and submitted reviews separately; a removed request may mean review completed.

options.name: draft to ready
options.decision_rule: Keep incomplete work draft; move ready when description, diff and checks support review. CODEOWNERS automatic requests happen on readiness.
options.verification: Re-read isDraft and automatic requests; explain review scope in the authorized PR description.

options.name: require_code_owner_reviews
options.decision_rule: Routing alone never enforces approval; enable enforcement where actual independent owners exist and repository rules call for it.
options.verification: Read effective protection/ruleset plus PR reviewDecision; avoid self-approval deadlock.

pitfalls: The author cannot approve their own PR. A single-maintainer repository may deliberately require zero peer approvals while retaining routing and required checks.

groups.title: Issue chooser and PR template routing
groups.applicability: User-facing or collaborative repositories; lightweight internal projects can use fewer forms.

options.name: chooser.blank_issues_enabled / contact_links
options.decision_rule: Keep an accessible path for unusual reports; route support and private vulnerabilities to actual staffed destinations.
options.verification: Render chooser as intended contributor; open every contact URL without submitting.

options.name: form.name / description / title
options.decision_rule: Separate reproducible defects from proposals only when triage differs; avoid prefixes duplicating structured type.
options.verification: Open every template on default branch and check readable chooser order and defaults.

options.name: form.labels / assignees / type
options.decision_rule: Reuse taxonomy; default assignees only when maintainers accept that responsibility; labels must already exist.
options.verification: Check available labels/types/assignees and inspect a permitted representative result.

options.name: form.projects
options.decision_rule: For external reporters prefer Project auto-add because template project insertion needs the submitter's write access to that Project.
options.verification: Verify with relevant contributor permission context; do not use maintainer success as outsider proof.

options.name: PR template selection
options.decision_rule: Use concise purpose/validation/risk prompts; multiple templates need an actual selection link/process, not an assumed automatic chooser.
options.verification: Open new-PR draft composer and test the intended template URL without posting.

options.name: inheritance / placement
options.decision_rule: Inventory inherited files before adding duplicates; default-branch placement controls normal chooser availability.
options.verification: Compare effective chooser and local/owner file sources, including casing and extension.

pitfalls: Issue forms become editable Markdown; required form controls are intake aids, not permanent structured-field enforcement. Issue forms are not PR forms.

groups.title: Nested form controls and validation
groups.applicability: For every configured YAML issue form; discussion forms reuse supported controls with their own top-level schema.

options.name: body[].type / id
options.decision_rule: Pick the control matching the answer; use stable unique IDs for supported prefills and future maintenance.
options.verification: Validate schema and render each control on the target host; require a non-markdown control.

options.name: input.attributes
options.decision_rule: Require actionable minimum information, not optional diagnostics; placeholders are examples, values are submitted defaults.
options.verification: Clear required inputs in preview and inspect validation behavior without posting.

options.name: textarea.attributes
options.decision_rule: Use render for literal logs/code only; omit it when Markdown editing or attachment affordances are needed.
options.verification: Check code-fence output and attachment/Markdown behavior in composer.

options.name: dropdown.attributes
options.decision_rule: Default only when the common choice is safe; use no default when choosing version/platform must be deliberate.
options.verification: Check unique options, index bounds, single versus multiple selection and empty validation.

options.name: checkboxes.attributes.options[]
options.decision_rule: Require only a meaningful acknowledgement; individual required flags differ from an optional checklist.
options.verification: Test unchecked required item and check rendered links and separate labels.

options.name: markdown / upload
options.decision_rule: Markdown guidance is not submitted content; keep critical reporting requirements in actual controls. Upload only needed files with privacy guidance.
options.verification: Preview target schema support; inspect attachment expectations and avoid requesting secrets.

pitfalls: Do not invent regex validators, conditional controls or arbitrary client logic; unsupported YAML keys can prevent the form appearing.

groups.title: Types, labels, owners and milestone planning
groups.applicability: Every tracked work item; owner-wide definitions only with owner-level applicability.

options.name: issue.type / owner definition
options.decision_rule: Prefer the owner's existing Bug/Task/Feature equivalents; types describe work kind rather than transient status. Owner edits affect other repositories.
options.verification: List owner and repository types, then read the issue's assigned type ID.

options.name: labels[] / label color-description
options.decision_rule: Labels serve useful cross-cutting queries; preserve customized names/colors and add/remove narrowly instead of replacing all.
options.verification: Compare before/after label ID sets and rendered descriptions; check saved filters still match renamed labels.

options.name: assignees[]
options.decision_rule: Assign a responsible person only when the task or project convention authorizes it; assignment does not mean acceptance.
options.verification: Check assignability then re-read the exact assignee set; do not confuse PR reviewer and assignee.

options.name: milestone.title / description / due_on / state
options.decision_rule: Use milestones for real releases/deadlines, not arbitrary duplicates of Project iterations; dates are targets.
options.verification: Read milestone counters and all included open/closed issues and PRs; closing milestone does not close work.

options.name: metadata mutation mode
options.decision_rule: Use delta mutations for focused edits; reserve replace for an explicitly reconciled full desired set.
options.verification: Re-read concurrent metadata before write and confirm unrelated labels/assignees remain.

pitfalls: Do not create a new taxonomy each run or use a label named Feature as proof native issue type is configured.

groups.title: Shared issue definitions and Project-local fields
groups.applicability: Cross-repository structured facts use owner issue fields; Project-only estimates/status use Project fields. Preview/host gates must be inspected.

options.name: field scope / applicability
options.decision_rule: Put reusable facts on the issue; Project issue-field cells are empty for PRs, draft items and issues from other owners.
options.verification: Read owner definition, issue sidebar and Project column as intended audience; missing applicability is not missing data.

options.name: visibility / API enum
options.decision_rule: Retain restricted default for nonpublic planning facts; public/internal Projects expose only Public issue fields. Changing to Restricted removes the field from those Projects.
options.verification: Read exact API visibility and inspect viewer/sidebar/timeline/Project behavior; do not change visibility merely to display a column.

options.name: pin to types / field limits
values: no pins; current 25 owner fields/100 select options/10 pins per type/50 total Project fields
options.decision_rule: Pin relevant fields so creation/view surfaces show them automatically; unpinned fields remain available through Add field and Projects. Limits differ from Project single-select options.
options.verification: Read pin mapping for typed and untyped issues and count all system/issue/local Project fields; verify target-host limits before creating.

options.name: data_type / typed value
options.decision_rule: Select type from actual schema; use date for dates and number for arithmetic, not formatted strings.
options.verification: Inspect supported owner and Project types separately; round-trip one permitted value of the selected type.

options.name: select options
options.decision_rule: Reuse IDs; rename in place when supported, never recreate populated options just to reorder or recolor.
options.verification: Export affected values before change and compare option IDs and representative assignments afterward.

options.name: issue field values operation
values: delete; typed scalar or option IDs
options.decision_rule: Preserve unrelated values and distinguish adding multi-select members from replacing the selected set.
options.verification: Read all current issue-field-values and compare exact changed field and option IDs.

options.name: intake population
options.decision_rule: Do not promise template or URL prefill of native issue fields; those are currently unsupported in the consulted product guide.
options.verification: Verify creation path then read the issue fields, not Markdown text that happens to have the same heading.

community_sources.observation: July 2026 community post describes multi-select preview; treat as discovery, not authority for every host or endpoint.
community_sources.official_check: Current issue-field-values examples include multi_select; bundled UpdateProjectV2FieldInput also exposes multiSelectOptions. Live entitlement remains untested.

pitfalls: A community preview announcement is not proof of API type support or entitlement. Inspect the exact host schema and actual rendered field.

groups.title: Completion, hierarchy, blockers and identity
groups.applicability: Issues with meaningful lifecycle; hierarchy/dependencies only where real decomposition/order exists.

options.name: state / state_reason
options.decision_rule: Close completed only with acceptance evidence; not-planned needs a decision reason; reopen the original issue for the same unfinished work.
options.verification: Read state/state_reason and timeline; closing is not deployment verification.

options.name: parent / child order
options.decision_rule: Use one parent for decomposition, preserve child identity and ordering; avoid manufacturing hierarchy for unrelated work.
options.verification: Read parent and child sides, all pages and final sibling order; current product limits are 100 children and eight levels.

options.name: blocked_by / blocking
options.decision_rule: Record A blocked by B when B must finish first; parenthood and a mention do not establish dependency.
options.verification: Query both directions and verify no self/cyclic/duplicate relationship accepted by the host.

options.name: related / duplicate
options.decision_rule: Link peers as related; point duplicates to the canonical issue and retain the reporter's reproduction details there by reference.
options.verification: Read canonical URLs and relationship timeline; do not delete duplicate history.

options.name: transfer / pin
options.decision_rule: Transfer only after access/ownership consequences are understood; use pins for durable current entry points, not every issue.
options.verification: Follow old URL, read new repository/number/ID, metadata and relationship preservation.

options.name: linkedBranch.repositoryId / name / oid
options.decision_rule: Start from observed default/base SHA unless task needs a release branch; link existing work before creating duplicate branches.
options.verification: Read actual ref OID and issue linkedBranches; link does not substitute for a closing PR.

options.name: planning status
options.decision_rule: Preview planning statuses may transition issue state; use only after discovering viewerCanSetStatus and available statuses.
options.verification: Read status plus open/closed state and duplicate target; do not equate it to Project Status.

pitfalls: Removal of a hierarchy/dependency edge is not deletion of either issue. Native relationships need actual API/UI evidence, not a checklist in the body.

groups.title: Human conversation and durable evidence
groups.applicability: Every task involving past decisions, edits, triage or review follow-up.

options.name: read model
options.decision_rule: Read all relevant streams before replying; issue body and last few visible comments omit decisions, force pushes, transfers and prior review outcomes.
options.verification: Independently paginate nested connections; reconcile IDs/timestamps and retrieve referenced objects.

options.name: edit versus append
options.decision_rule: Edit the canonical description to reflect current scope; append material decisions and corrections when authorized so reasoning remains chronological.
options.verification: Compare prior content and edit history where available; retain earlier evidence URLs and authorship.

options.name: comment/reply location
options.decision_rule: Reply in the thread containing the question; distinguish implemented fix, justified disagreement, unresolved question and deferred follow-up.
options.verification: Read thread root/reply IDs and resulting thread state; never claim a pending review was delivered.

options.name: notifications / mentions
options.decision_rule: Mention only relevant people when an authorized message needs their attention; do not silently change watch/subscription settings.
options.verification: Inspect recipient and final posted location; API success is not proof the user read the message.

options.name: attachments / artifacts
options.decision_rule: Preserve attachment identity and permissions; reference existing logs/files instead of re-uploading private content publicly.
options.verification: Verify readable content with permitted audience and identify expiry; attachment presence is not content validation.

options.name: recovery after ambiguous write
options.decision_rule: Avoid duplicate posts after timeouts; inspect recent author/timestamp/body and relationship events before retry.
options.verification: Capture canonical ID/URL and distinguish already-applied from unapplied writes.

community_sources.observation: Long-running reports describe collapsed older activity and difficult navigation; exact UI behavior has changed over time.
community_sources.official_check: REST timeline and comment endpoints are separately paginated, so use their complete relevant pages rather than infer completeness from the rendered screen.

community_sources.observation: Users seek issue/comment edit history through APIs and point to GraphQL.
community_sources.official_check: Inspect UserContentEdit connections and viewer permissions on the current schema; do not claim a comments list contains every revision.

pitfalls: Git history is not conversation history; activity feeds are not complete audit logs. Loading an old thread in UI may collapse large portions.

groups.title: PR intent, comparison base and connected work
groups.applicability: All code changes delivered through PRs; native stacks/archival only on supported hosts.

options.name: head / base / draft
options.decision_rule: Discover existing PR before creating; choose correct target release/default branch and draft state from readiness.
options.verification: Read head repo/ref/SHA, base ref/SHA and isDraft; inspect full diff against merge base.

options.name: title / body / maintainer_can_modify
options.decision_rule: Describe final scope and evidence; allow fork-maintainer edits only when contributor intent and repository trust permit.
options.verification: Re-read rendered description and fork edit permission; retain rationale and linked decisions.

options.name: closing keyword / manual development link
options.decision_rule: Use closing intent only for fully satisfied issues targeting default branch; use plain references for partial work or release-target PRs.
options.verification: Check development links before merge, issue state and timeline after merge; commit-only closing may omit PR sidebar linkage.

options.name: base retarget / branch rewrite
options.decision_rule: Recheck scope before retargeting; changing base can remove visible commits and make inline comments outdated. Preserve decision URLs and communicate material scope changes in authorized flow.
options.verification: Compare old/new base/head SHAs, diff, review freshness and unresolved/outdated threads.

options.name: native stack / archival
options.decision_rule: Use native stack support only where available; archive is distinct from close, branch deletion and Project archive.
options.verification: Read actual stack/base relationships or archived/state fields and timeline; do not simulate support with text and label it configured.

pitfalls: A PR references the live head branch; pushing after review changes the material under review. Closing without merge does not mean delivered.

groups.title: Review decisions, anchors, pending state and resolution
groups.applicability: All review work; submitted comments are external messages and require task authorization.

options.name: review.commit_id / event
options.decision_rule: Bind evidence to the reviewed head. Draft/pending reviews are private; submit only the intended decision and explain actionable findings.
options.verification: Read review ID, commit_id, state, submitted_at and comments; author cannot approve own PR.

options.name: inline anchor
options.decision_rule: Anchor to an actual diff on the observed SHA; prefer current line/side coordinates, not deprecated positional guessing.
options.verification: Re-read comment diff_hunk, original/current line and commit IDs; wrong anchor requires correction, not silent relocation.

options.name: reply and suggestion
options.decision_rule: Preserve original conversation; inspect suggestions as code, batch related accepted edits and verify new commits.
options.verification: Read replies and resulting branch SHA; rerun affected checks after applying suggestions.

options.name: viewed files / diff settings
options.decision_rule: Viewed is personal progress, not approval; inspect whitespace when meaningful and unmark changed files requiring another pass.
options.verification: Read viewerViewedState as same viewer and current path/head; record what was actually reviewed.

options.name: thread.resolve / reopen
options.decision_rule: Resolve after code/evidence addresses the finding or recorded agreement; outdated merely means anchor drift, not fixed.
options.verification: Read isResolved/isOutdated and implementing commit or linked follow-up; preserve unresolved material objections.

options.name: dismissal.message / restrictions
options.decision_rule: Dismiss only invalidated/unavailable-reviewer feedback with an explicit reason and policy authority; do not erase dissent to unblock merge.
options.verification: Read dismissed review state and timeline rationale plus remaining effective review requirements.

pitfalls: Review comments, issue-style PR comments and commit comments are different stores. Never respond to only the summary while missing inline threads.

groups.title: Merge settings and asynchronous delivery
groups.applicability: Repositories accepting merges; queue/auto-merge/Agent Merge only where supported and justified by throughput.

options.name: allow_merge_commit / allow_squash_merge / allow_rebase_merge
options.decision_rule: Follow existing history policy and effective branch rules; retain squash-only delivery where the repository policy requires it. Avoid introducing several methods without a reason.
options.verification: Read repository flags and allowed methods in effective rules; inspect actual resulting commit topology.

options.name: squash_merge_commit_title / message
values: PR_TITLE or COMMIT_OR_PR_TITLE; PR_BODY or COMMIT_MESSAGES or BLANK
options.decision_rule: Prefer stable PR title plus reviewed useful body for a one-change PR; inspect generated message for accidental skip directives or sensitive diagnostics.
options.verification: Preview final message and read resulting commit; verify expected CI ran on the merged SHA.

options.name: merge_commit_title / message
values: PR_TITLE or MERGE_MESSAGE; PR_BODY or PR_TITLE or BLANK
options.decision_rule: If merge commits are enabled, choose a useful durable description without dumping transient logs.
options.verification: Read supported enum payload and final commit message; no configuration claim from preview alone.

options.name: merge.sha / merge_method
options.decision_rule: Guard the merge against concurrent head changes; do not override required checks, outstanding review or queue to satisfy a local plan.
options.verification: Re-read current head and gate state, then resulting merged flag, merge_commit_sha and base ref.

options.name: auto-merge / queue entry
options.decision_rule: Enable only for reviewed intent and qualifying rules; enqueue/enable is pending work, not completion.
options.verification: Poll meaningful state changes until merge/failure or handoff; inspect queue removal reason and merged commit checks.

options.name: update_branch.expected_head_sha / delete_branch_on_merge / revert
options.decision_rule: Update only after inspecting divergence; delete truly merged disposable branches, retain long-lived branches. Revert through a tracked PR rather than history rewrite.
options.verification: Confirm head after update, branch absent only when intended, and revert result against merged commit.

community_sources.observation: A path-trigger investigation traced missing Actions runs to skip directives copied into a squash commit message.
community_sources.official_check: Official skip-workflow and squash-message documentation explains the mechanism. Inspect final message and run checks; do not conclude squash inherently breaks path filters.

pitfalls: Squash of a reused long-lived branch can replay prior commits in later PRs; start a fresh branch. Agent-merge eligibility must be checked separately.

groups.title: Project scope, access and item identity
groups.applicability: Use Projects where the repository workflow calls for planning/tracking; public/private and organization/user ownership remain explicit choices.

options.name: owner / number / node ID
options.decision_rule: Reuse an existing matching Project; store owner/number/URL and node ID, never treat repository Projects flag as owner Project setup.
options.verification: Read Project owner/ID/title/closed/public and linked repository list.

options.name: visibility / base permission / explicit collaborators
options.decision_rule: Choose least privilege for the real audience; repository access and Project access are separate. Draft titles and custom data can expose information.
options.verification: Read base/explicit grants and inspect as intended reader; do not broaden repo access to make a Project readable.

options.name: item content type / IDs
values: DraftIssue; item ID distinct from content ID
options.decision_rule: Keep tracked work as native issues/PRs; draft ideas are appropriate before a repository is selected. Reuse existing item for content ID.
options.verification: Paginate items and match content node ID/URL, including archived entries.

options.name: draft conversion
options.decision_rule: Convert when the work has a responsible repository; preserve draft body, relevant fields and links, and check access before conversion.
options.verification: Read returned issue URL and item content type/field values; do not create a second item for the same work.

options.name: item reorder / archive / delete
options.decision_rule: Use archive for recoverable history; deletion removes membership/field data, not the underlying issue.
options.verification: Compare item IDs and saved values; restore archive when needed and verify representative fields.

community_sources.observation: April 2026 report shows successful CLI add and issue association while list/UI omit the item.
community_sources.official_check: Treat as incident evidence, not a current general guarantee. Read actual item by ID, paginate, inspect archive/filter and relevant repository access before retrying.

pitfalls: Successful item-add is not proof that every view will show it: filters, archives, pagination, permissions or a service incident can hide the item.

groups.title: Project field configuration and value integrity
groups.applicability: Every Project; additional fields only when a real view, query or decision uses them.

options.name: field data type / semantic scope
options.decision_rule: Reuse built-in title/assignee/type/milestone and shared issue facts; create local fields only for Project-specific planning.
options.verification: Inventory field IDs/types and example values; distinguish issue fields from similar-name local fields.

options.name: Status options / order / default
values: discovered IDs; e.g. Todo/In Progress/Done; optional default
options.decision_rule: Retain established names/IDs and explicitly define completion. Default to intake/Todo only if all newly added work is truly queued.
options.verification: Read options/default and a newly added versus existing item; default changes must not silently rewrite old work.

options.name: select label / description / color
options.decision_rule: Give ambiguous statuses a usable entry/exit definition; preserve IDs across cosmetic changes. Colors supplement text, never replace meaning.
options.verification: Compare option IDs before/after, sampled assignments and UI descriptions; inspect schema before option-list replacement.

options.name: field mutation payload
options.decision_rule: Send exactly the relevant value member using discovered IDs; clearing a field is a separate intentional action.
options.verification: Read the changed field value and verify unrelated values remain; preserve zero versus unset.

options.name: field deletion / option removal
options.decision_rule: Migrate populated values before any authorized deletion; export mapping because recreating the same name may not recover identity.
options.verification: Compare all affected item values and saved-view/filter/workflow references; never prove safety using only one empty item.

pitfalls: Current single-select guide documents at most 50 options and an optional default for newly added items; target API/UI default support still requires discovery.

groups.title: Iteration schedules and rollover
groups.applicability: Only projects with real cadence; continuous-flow work does not need artificial sprints.

options.name: iteration configuration
options.decision_rule: Match the actual team's planning cadence and timezone assumptions; do not auto-create indefinite schedules.
options.verification: Read configuration plus automatically created iterations and exact IDs/dates.

options.name: iteration instance
options.decision_rule: Preserve completed iteration identity and assignments; amend future dates deliberately rather than shifting historical interpretation.
options.verification: Compare old/new date ranges and representative assigned work.

options.name: breaks
options.decision_rule: Reflect actual holidays/pauses; inspect generated dates after insertion rather than assuming later schedule is unchanged.
options.verification: Re-read all affected intervals and check no unintended overlap or shifted promised dates.

options.name: rollover
options.decision_rule: Move only unfinished selected work when agreed; keep prior commitment context in authorized update/history instead of silently rewriting all scope.
options.verification: Compare item IDs/status and previous/target iteration assignments, including nonselected completed work.

pitfalls: An iteration field initially creates three iterations; a break initially follows the prior duration. Product defaults are starting data, not a planning decision.

groups.title: View identity, shared configuration and safe filters
groups.applicability: Every Project with distinct intake, execution or reporting audiences; avoid duplicate views with no distinct purpose.

options.name: view name / layout / position
options.decision_rule: Name views by the decision they support, e.g. Intake, Active work, Release roadmap; set default/first useful view for readers.
options.verification: Read every saved view and reload shared URL, including ordering and unsaved-change indicators.

options.name: filter scope
values: repo/is/reason/assignee/label/type and custom field qualifiers supported in view
options.decision_rule: Store exact query, not a prose claim; include explicit repo/type/state where needed and quote multiword names.
options.verification: Check representative included/excluded items and zero-value/unassigned cases; a filter is not an access boundary.

options.name: number/date/iteration comparison
options.decision_rule: Use date/iteration semantics of this surface, not issue-search syntax; check boundary and timezone behavior with known values.
options.verification: Inspect edge dates and missing values; compare returned content IDs to expected fixtures/current known items.

options.name: view save / duplicate / reset / delete
options.decision_rule: Save intended shared configuration explicitly; use a duplicate for experimentation and do not delete a view with active shared links casually.
options.verification: Reopen as reader/new session and check persistent configuration and old navigation links.

options.name: API versus UI
options.decision_rule: Discover actual supported request fields; REST creation and GraphQL view CRUD exist, so avoid blanket UI-only claims.
options.verification: Read saved configuration through supported surface; use rendered verification for unsupported controls.

pitfalls: Auto-add and auto-archive have narrower filter grammars than views. A valid view query cannot be copied blindly into automation.

groups.title: Table and board nested controls
groups.applicability: For every table or board view that is part of the project workflow.

options.name: visible fields / column order / card fields
options.decision_rule: Show owner, status and the facts needed for this view; hide unused noise while preserving stored data.
options.verification: Reload saved view and inspect expected header/card fields and order.

options.name: board column field / visible columns / limits
options.decision_rule: Use Status for execution, iteration for planning; hide columns only with an alternate way to find excluded work. Column limits are planning signals, not enforcement.
options.verification: Verify field ID and value-to-column mapping; inspect hidden/no-value work and displayed limits.

options.name: group by / vertical_group_by
options.decision_rule: Group by responsible person, parent or priority for a real triage question; dragging across groups can edit underlying fields.
options.verification: Read fields after an authorized drag and verify parent/assignee effects rather than assuming presentation-only movement.

options.name: slice by
options.decision_rule: Use for fast per-team/repository focus; title/reviewers/linked PRs are not supported slice fields in current guide.
options.verification: Check slice plus saved filter intersection and clear selection to recover full view.

options.name: sort primary/secondary / direction
options.decision_rule: Use priority/date order when that drives work, manual order for explicit ranking; sorted boards disallow manual ordering within columns.
options.verification: Read saved sorting and known equal-value tie examples; distinguish drag-to-column mutation from reorder.

options.name: field sums
options.decision_rule: Sum only compatible measures; points are estimates and mixed currencies/units must not be combined.
options.verification: Recompute a representative group from actual item values and compare displayed aggregate.

pitfalls: Grouping a multi-assignee issue can show it in several groups; avoid interpreting row/card counts as unique work without checking IDs.

groups.title: Roadmap dates, markers and time windows
groups.applicability: Projects with dates or iteration commitments; omit when no credible schedule exists.

options.name: Date fields.Start date / Target date
values: chosen date or iteration field IDs
options.decision_rule: Bind to explicit planning fields, not guessed names; distinguish planned dates from actual completion evidence.
options.verification: Read both mappings and compare bar boundaries to item values; inspect undated work separately.

options.name: Markers
options.decision_rule: Display only useful commitment/reference markers to avoid implying every date is a release deadline.
options.verification: Inspect labels and actual source milestone/date values.

options.name: Zoom
options.decision_rule: Choose the smallest window supporting the planning decision; preserve a useful shared overview.
options.verification: Reload view and inspect expected time window and clipped/offscreen work.

options.name: roadmap drag / resize
values: changes start/target dates or selected iteration
options.decision_rule: Treat dragging as a real scheduling mutation; avoid accidental date changes during inspection.
options.verification: Read changed field values and affected automation afterward; restore exact original values on accidental edit.

options.name: group / slice / sort / sums
options.decision_rule: Apply the same data-integrity rules as other layouts; maintain access to ungrouped/undated items through a table view.
options.verification: Compare item IDs across roadmap and table to explain omissions without inventing missing work.

pitfalls: A visually complete roadmap can exclude undated items; never equate visible bars with all project scope.

groups.title: Event-driven Status transitions and issue closure
groups.applicability: Every Project, including apparently unconfigured Projects; defaults can already be active.

options.name: workflow enabled / target field-option
options.decision_rule: Inventory every built-in event workflow before manual reconciliation; retain behavior only when transition matches the project's definition.
options.verification: Read workflow trigger/enabled/target and verify a permitted representative transition.

options.name: item added → Status
options.decision_rule: Default new work to intake if untriaged; do not overwrite imported/customized existing work as a setup side effect.
options.verification: Observe new item value, existing populated item and applicable field default together.

options.name: issue/PR closed → Done
options.decision_rule: Closed-not-planned is not successful delivery; decide whether one Done column intentionally includes cancellation or needs separate reporting.
options.verification: Check reason and resulting Status for completed and not-planned examples; correct mismatches without reopening rejected work.

options.name: PR merged → Done
options.decision_rule: Merge may be completion for library work, but deployed systems may still require QA/release. Define that boundary explicitly.
options.verification: Read merged commit, item Status and downstream release/deployment evidence separately.

options.name: Status change → issue state
values: close issue on configured transition where supported
options.decision_rule: Enable only when board transitions truly authorize closing the issue; avoid circular/competing automation.
options.verification: Read issue state/reason and both directions of workflow behavior; identify unexpected loops or last-writer wins.

options.name: reopen / ready / review-related events
options.decision_rule: Inventory actual available triggers and decide each applicability rather than assume all event workflows exist everywhere.
options.verification: Read current workflow list/schema/UI and verify exact resulting option IDs after relevant event.

pitfalls: Initialization enables closed→Done and merged→Done. A successful Status write can be immediately changed by another workflow; verify after automation settles.

groups.title: Auto-add filters, backfill and execution identity
groups.applicability: For repository intake needing reliable Project membership; custom Actions only for unsupported native needs.

options.name: auto-add.repository / filter
options.decision_rule: Scope to intended repository and item kind; exclude automation noise deliberately. Validate native grammar independently of view query.
options.verification: Read enabled workflow and exact filter; inspect a matching and a nonmatching permitted item.

options.name: filter values / negation
options.decision_rule: Use supported values and negation (no does not support negation); quote labels. Do not invent arbitrary custom-field auto-add filters.
options.verification: Preview/save and confirm actual matching content IDs; compare available grammar with current official guide.

options.name: workflow count / duplicate
options.decision_rule: Reuse existing workflows; Free has one, Pro/Team five, Enterprise twenty in current guide. Record plan gate rather than adding a token workaround silently.
options.verification: Read actual count and entitlement; verify each repository selector and duplicate filter.

options.name: existing backlog
options.decision_rule: Enabling auto-add does not backfill existing matches; reconcile backlog as a separate authorized operation preserving item values.
options.verification: List source issues/PRs, compare content IDs to active/archive membership and add only missing items.

options.name: custom Action identity
values: installation token or authorized user credential
options.decision_rule: Repository GITHUB_TOKEN generally cannot stand in for owner Project write access; prefer a scoped App only when native workflow is insufficient.
options.verification: Inspect workflow/token permissions without exposing secrets; verify membership and typed field values after execution.

pitfalls: Creating a dummy issue to test automation sends real notifications and is not a read-only check; use existing evidence or an explicitly authorized representative fixture.

groups.title: Retention filters, existing matches and restoration
groups.applicability: Projects with a defined retention policy; keep disabled if release/QA remains open after issue closure.

options.name: auto-archive.enabled / filter
options.decision_rule: Prefer disabled until retention criteria are agreed; custom Status is not supported in this automation grammar.
options.verification: Read exact saved filter and enabled state; enumerate matching existing items before enable.

options.name: retention clock
values: updated relative-date expression supported by current surface
options.decision_rule: Do not call last-updated age closed-age; comments/labels/assignees/milestones/field changes can reset update time.
options.verification: Test known boundary examples in this automation surface; record literal filter rather than translating comparator from memory.

options.name: existing matches
values: immediately eligible after enable, potentially delayed processing
options.decision_rule: Inventory affected IDs/values first; unlike auto-add, auto-archive also processes old matching items.
options.verification: Compare before/after active and archive IDs and counts until processing settles.

options.name: archive versus capacity
options.decision_rule: Archive keeps custom data and supports restore but still counts toward current 50,000 combined item limit. Deletion needs a separate retention decision.
options.verification: Read archive entries and restored values; verify underlying issue remains unchanged.

options.name: recovery
options.decision_rule: Stop faulty automation first, restore exact affected items and values, then correct filter before re-enabling.
options.verification: Re-read saved filter and representative restored fields; inspect re-archival to detect remaining bad criteria.

community_sources.observation: Historical reports include unsupported Status filters, unexpected archive effects and confusing recovery.
community_sources.official_check: Current guide restricts filters to is/reason/updated and documents preservation/restoration. Use those verified limits rather than obsolete 1,200-item claims.

community_sources.observation: Users ask for closed-date retention and suggest updated-based workarounds.
community_sources.official_check: Updated and closed time are different clocks; do not repeat a community workaround as exact closure retention.

pitfalls: Historical Community reports describe invalid filters partly executing; do not present that old bug as current. Validate native grammar and preserve a restoration inventory.

groups.title: Charts, historical interpretation and project health
groups.applicability: Projects where someone consumes the report; do not create decorative metrics or post updates without authorization.

options.name: chart filter / layout / X-axis / group
options.decision_rule: Name the actual decision and denominator; chart filters are their own saved configuration, not inherited proof from an open view.
options.verification: Open saved chart and compare included content IDs/known sample; verify reader access.

options.name: Y-axis / numeric field
options.decision_rule: Count unique work or aggregate compatible numeric units; never equate estimate sums with actual labor or outcome value.
options.verification: Recompute sample groups including missing/zero values and inspect saved aggregate and field mapping.

options.name: historical chart state / retention
values: Time axis; Open/Completed/Closed pull requests/Not planned
options.decision_rule: Historical charts track native issue/PR states, not arbitrary local Status history. Insights does not track archived or deleted items, so retention affects reporting.
options.verification: Compare known state transitions and active/archive membership; do not report archive-filtered history as all-time delivery.

options.name: status update.status
options.decision_rule: Set overall project health from evidence, separately from issue open/closed and item Status; meaningful bad news must remain visible.
options.verification: Read saved update ID/status and chronological update history.

options.name: status update.startDate / targetDate / body
options.decision_rule: Include reason, evidence and next decision; inspect inherited previous dates rather than republish stale commitments. Append meaningful updates, edit only corrections.
options.verification: Read resulting dates/body and prior entries; templates cannot receive updates and subscriptions can notify readers.

pitfalls: Chart controls may require UI even when field/view APIs exist. Do not claim chart configuration from project item listing or API capability indexing.

groups.title: Template/copy fidelity and initial conditions
groups.applicability: Repeated project patterns; do not create a template where one Project already suffices.

options.name: copy owner / title / draft selection
options.decision_rule: Choose destination deliberately and copy example drafts only when useful; inspect template contents for confidential planning text.
options.verification: Read new owner/title/ID and copied draft bodies/values.

options.name: copied configuration
options.decision_rule: Treat copied settings as a starting point, not desired final state; inherited automation can immediately affect new work.
options.verification: Compare each copied component and field-option mappings independently with source snapshot.

options.name: not copied
options.decision_rule: Recreate only applicable omitted relationships and intake workflow under authorized access scope; backfill existing work separately.
options.verification: Read membership, grants, links and enabled auto-add on destination; source configuration proves nothing about destination completion.

options.name: organization template / recommendations
options.decision_rule: Curate only usable templates with documented fields and workflow expectations; avoid promoting an unverified personal experiment.
options.verification: Read template status and organization recommendation visibility as intended member.

pitfalls: Copied field/option IDs are destination identities; never apply source item/field IDs to the new Project by name alone.

groups.title: Discussion purposes, category formats and intake
groups.applicability: Public/community projects or genuinely cross-repository decisions; small internal work can stay in issues.

options.name: repository versus organization source
options.decision_rule: Keep repo-specific support near code; organization-wide discussions need explicit source-repository governance and access review.
options.verification: Read enabled surface, source repository and moderator roles; inspect audience before publishing.

options.name: category.name / emoji / description / format
options.decision_rule: Use Q&A for answerable support, open-ended for design, announcement for maintainer-origin updates. Inspect current Polls control rather than treating docs prose inconsistencies as universal support.
options.verification: Read category IDs and actual format/answerability; announcement posting has stricter permissions than replies.

options.name: section membership / category rename/delete
options.decision_rule: Reuse category IDs; preserve navigation and discussion history. Deleting a category moves discussions to a chosen existing category.
options.verification: Compare IDs/format and counts, destination and old shared links; inspect forms after slug changes.

options.name: category form path / top-level schema
options.decision_rule: Match category slug exactly; use supported controls, not issue-form assignee/projects/type top-level keys.
options.verification: Open actual category composer on default branch and validate required/non-Markdown fields without posting.

options.name: labels / pins
options.decision_rule: Pin actionable entry points with a moderator/response owner; avoid a duplicate label taxonomy.
options.verification: Read pin location, appearance and rendered routing links; global pins and category pins are distinct.

options.name: category movement / poll intake
options.decision_rule: Select a valid format before intake; do not promise migration of a normal topic into a poll by changing category.
options.verification: Read current category/format and eligible destinations; preserve original topic links.

pitfalls: Enabling Discussions creates a surface, not a staffed support process. Define who monitors unanswered questions and how decisions become tracked work.

groups.title: Answers, polls, conversions and moderation history
groups.applicability: Every authorized discussion interaction; high-impact moderation requires exact task scope.

options.name: answer selection
options.decision_rule: Mark a correct reusable solution with supporting explanation; an accepted answer is not proof a linked implementation shipped.
options.verification: Read answer ID/body/author and category answerability; retain unresolved follow-up.

options.name: reply hierarchy / poll vote
options.decision_rule: Respond to the right question; inspect existing viewer vote and options. Voting is personal participation, not setup.
options.verification: Read reply parent and viewer vote state/counts; never cast a vote merely to test a feature.

options.name: poll content
values: at least two options in Polls composer
options.decision_rule: Choose clear distinct options and explain how feedback informs a decision; do not invent supported close dates, anonymity or binding voting rules.
options.verification: Preview composer and read poll question/options/order after an authorized creation; creation API support needs its own discovery.

options.name: lock / close / reason / allow reactions
options.decision_rule: Prefer explanation and narrow moderation; lock restricts interaction while preserving content. Do not silence technical disagreement.
options.verification: Read locked/closed/reason and rendered notice; confirm permitted moderators and reactions separately.

options.name: issue → discussion conversion
values: original issue and resulting discussion IDs
options.decision_rule: Use only when conversation rather than committed work is appropriate; explain routing when messaging is authorized and snapshot original history first.
options.verification: Read both objects, canonical links, authors, all comment/reaction pages and issue closure/lock behavior; reconcile timeout before retry.

options.name: create issue from discussion
values: linked new issue in responsible repository
options.decision_rule: Track accepted actionable work while retaining the discussion decision trail; do not assume participants/subscriptions or every metadata field move.
options.verification: Read both cross-links and preserve original authors and decision context.

options.name: transfer discussion
values: eligible same-owner destination repository or organization source repo
options.decision_rule: Destination creation permission is required; private-to-public and announcement transfers are unsupported. Review audience before any allowed transfer.
options.verification: Read destination repository/category/access and retained comments/links; reconcile original and returned discussion IDs.

options.name: minimize / delete
options.decision_rule: Use least destructive appropriate moderation with reason; deletion is not a substitute for marking superseded information.
options.verification: Read minimized state or exact deleted ID and preserve required moderation rationale without redistributing sensitive content.

community_sources.observation: February 2025 conversion-to-404 incident was reported fixed by GitHub staff in March 2025.
community_sources.official_check: Current moderation docs describe conversion; verify each resulting object and retained comments rather than treat this as a present platform outage.

community_sources.observation: Maintainers describe user confusion about converted issues becoming closed/locked and request clearer traceability.
community_sources.official_check: Use current official flow plus actual post-conversion reads; communicate destination and preserve the old decision trail when authorized.

community_sources.observation: Long history includes contradictory conversion advice and assumptions about participant/watch preservation.
community_sources.official_check: Official current docs, not a recent unverified forum reply, determine supported flow; inspect destination authors/comments/access independently.

pitfalls: Community conversion threads contain conflicting claims and historical incidents. Current official conversion flow exists; do not repeat a claim that conversion is universally unavailable.

groups.title: Wiki content, publication, permissions and discoverability
groups.applicability: Projects needing a Wiki; separate site/Pages only when user need justifies it.

options.name: enabled / editing audience
values: public editing on eligible public repos
options.decision_rule: Default to repository writers for project policy/docs; public editing is a governance choice, not a completeness requirement.
options.verification: Read repository flag and actual Wiki access control; public/private visibility follows repository audience.

options.name: source repository / publication ref
options.decision_rule: Clone/fetch Wiki separately; preserve other contributors' commits and compare source wiki/ files before publishing.
options.verification: Compare remote before/after commit SHA and rendered pages; source files alone are not proof of publication.

options.name: page title / filename / markup
options.decision_rule: Keep page naming stable and explicit; avoid filesystem case collisions and check renamed-page backlinks.
options.verification: Render pages and follow links on GitHub, inspect separate Wiki Git log and page history.

options.name: navigation
options.decision_rule: Provide install/use/config/troubleshooting navigation based on actual project scope; footer can carry source/version context.
options.verification: Open every navigation destination, heading anchor and asset as intended reader.

options.name: change message / correction / recovery
options.decision_rule: Record what changed and why; recover with a new corrective commit rather than force-overwrite others' Wiki work.
options.verification: Read remote ancestry and page revision, compare preserved unrelated pages and restored content.

options.name: indexing / size constraints
options.decision_rule: Do not promise search-engine discovery for a small Wiki; current guide requires 500 stars and restricted public editing, with soft 5,000-file limit.
options.verification: Inspect actual audience/search behavior; consider Pages only if indexing or size is an actual requirement.

pitfalls: A main-repository pull request does not review/enforce separate Wiki pushes automatically; document the publication check and do not conflate branches.

groups.title: Search surfaces, query semantics and completeness
groups.applicability: Discovery before every duplicate-sensitive operation; authoritative owning endpoints for final facts.

options.name: code search surface
options.decision_rule: Choose syntax for the actual engine; browser Boolean/regex/symbol features do not imply equivalent REST support. Use local Git for exact nondefault-revision inspection.
options.verification: Record engine, repository and revision; retrieve matched file at immutable SHA before acting.

options.name: modern code query
options.decision_rule: Scope narrowly and escape literals correctly; a bare term can match path or content. Inspect actual engine limits before assuming exhaustive indexing.
options.verification: Reproduce match locally at known revision and inspect excluded files/ref; empty search is not absence proof.

options.name: issue/PR query
options.decision_rule: Use explicit type and repository scope, native review qualifiers for review queues and dates for bounded investigations.
options.verification: Retrieve every consequential issue/PR by ID and paginate authoritative collection for completeness.

options.name: Discussion query
options.decision_rule: Search existing answers/decisions before creating a new topic; category and issue-search grammars differ.
options.verification: Open original discussion, current answer and full relevant replies; check date of claim and superseding staff response.

options.name: REST search result limits
options.decision_rule: Treat results as indexed discovery; split disjoint date/repository ranges and reconcile total counts when cap or incompleteness appears.
options.verification: Inspect incomplete_results and available pages, deduplicate IDs; use owning lists/GraphQL/Git if a full inventory is required.

options.name: saved queries / issue views
options.decision_rule: Save useful triage/review queries with explicit audience; a personal saved search is not a shared Project view.
options.verification: Reload as same viewer, inspect exact query and validate known expected item membership.

pitfalls: Masked private objects, indexing lag, engine-specific limits and search caps mean zero results cannot establish absence or permission. Never use obsolete legacy limits as modern Code Search limits.

groups.title: Ruleset scope, bypass and evaluation evidence
groups.applicability: Every repository audit; enforce only with repository policy, eligible plan and a tested contribution path.

options.name: target / conditions
values: push; ref_name include/exclude; repository targeting at owner scope
options.decision_rule: Inspect inherited rules and select exact intended ref patterns, including default-branch symbolic selectors when supported; exclusion can silently remove protection.
options.verification: Read ruleset IDs/source/enforcement plus effective rules for a representative matching and excluded ref.

options.name: enforcement
options.decision_rule: Disabled protects nothing; evaluate observes without blocking and needs a plan check. Preview broad new policy in evaluate where available before enforcement.
options.verification: Read saved mode and rule-suite results; do not report evaluate as protected.

options.name: bypass_actors.actor_type / actor_id / bypass_mode
options.decision_rule: Preserve existing authorized exceptions and choose the narrowest useful mode; exempt does not run rules or create a bypass audit entry.
options.verification: Read actor identity/mode and confirm no accidental broad role exception or App removal.

options.name: rule suite filters
options.decision_rule: Inspect operational failures and bypass use, not merely policy JSON. Check current endpoint filter enums and retention before querying.
options.verification: Read suite ID, actor, ref, evaluation time and per-rule result; distinguish evaluate failures from blocked writes.

options.name: ruleset history / import-export
options.decision_rule: Preserve baseline/version and review imported selectors/actor IDs; source owner IDs do not automatically mean destination identities.
options.verification: Compare saved ruleset history, exact imported payload and effective target rules; revert with a corrective version.

pitfalls: Multiple rulesets can apply together with classic protection. A clear ruleset read does not prove the actor had no bypass or that another inherited rule did not apply.

groups.title: Effective review/check requirements and compatible merge behavior
groups.applicability: All protected default/release branches; single-maintainer workflows must not require impossible self-approval.

options.name: required_pull_request_reviews
options.decision_rule: Choose actual independent reviewer availability; stale/last-push rules must match team workflow. Zero peer approval may be intentional with required checks.
options.verification: Read effective rules and representative current-head review states; inspect reviewer eligibility and outstanding changes requests.

options.name: review dismissal / bypass restrictions
options.decision_rule: Retain narrowly justified emergency routes; never add the running agent as bypass to complete setup.
options.verification: Compare actor IDs and enabled restrictions, and inspect subsequent dismissal/bypass evidence.

options.name: required_status_checks
options.decision_rule: Bind stable check names to expected Apps where supported; strict requires up-to-date branch, queue needs merge_group CI support.
options.verification: Compare rules to actual check-run names/App IDs on PR and merge-group SHAs; skipped or pending is not passing.

options.name: enforce_admins / restrictions
options.decision_rule: Decide administrator policy deliberately; push allowlists are not equivalent to review bypass. Preserve existing emergency ownership.
options.verification: Read protection and ruleset bypass together; verify effective actor rights without making a disruptive test push.

options.name: history / signatures / deletion
options.decision_rule: Match legitimate release workflow and retain no-force/no-delete for protected history unless specifically justified. Locked branches and fork-sync settings need separate intent.
options.verification: Read all flags and branch status; verify merge methods remain compatible with linear history.

options.name: conversation/deployment/security gates
options.decision_rule: Require gates only when their producer/workflow exists and can complete; determine exact environment/tool thresholds from the schema and project policy.
options.verification: Read named environments/tool thresholds and current-head gate results; do not disable failing gates as recovery.

options.name: repository merge flags
options.decision_rule: Keep methods compatible with effective rules; auto-update visibility is not auto-merge or branch freshness. Clean only disposable merged heads.
options.verification: Read repository flags and PR merge box/effective rule methods; inspect final merge topology and branch cleanup.

options.name: merge queue parameters
options.decision_rule: Use only when contention justifies it; inspect current host schema for exact names/enums and ensure queue check triggers exist.
options.verification: Read queue rule payload and representative merge_group results, queue removal reasons and merged SHA.

pitfalls: Classic protection update endpoints can replace nested objects and clear omitted policy. Snapshot and merge intended changes; one protected-branch endpoint cannot establish full ruleset enforcement.

groups.title: Personal watch choices, inbox triage and feed limitations
groups.applicability: Only the authenticated user’s authorized personal preferences; repository setup does not authorize following/watching or marking inbox items done.

options.name: repository subscription
values: custom event selection through supported UI
options.decision_rule: Preserve user preference; watch only requested event categories and distinguish ignored from simply not subscribed. Stars bookmark rather than subscribe.
options.verification: Read subscription as same user plus UI custom categories; subscribers_count differs from legacy watchers_count/stargazers_count.

options.name: watcher list restrictions
options.decision_rule: Current docs describe July 2026 restrictions and deprecated endpoint empty responses; do not infer nobody watches from an empty legacy list.
options.verification: Check endpoint status/auth identity and direct repository subscription state.

options.name: inbox query
options.decision_rule: Choose smallest needed read window and paginate; inspect reason such as mention/review_request/assign rather than treating all notifications equally.
options.verification: Read thread ID/subject/reason/unread/last_read_at and canonical owning object.

options.name: triage operation
options.decision_rule: Read acknowledges visibility; done hides completed notifications, save retains attention, unsubscribe changes future delivery. Apply only explicitly intended selected threads.
options.verification: Re-read selected thread and UI saved/done state; compare unaffected threads, and reconcile ambiguous writes before retry.

options.name: retention / subscription recovery
options.decision_rule: Inbox is not permanent project history; unsaving old notifications can make them disappear. Unsubscribe can be superseded by later mention or review request.
options.verification: Preserve canonical issue/PR URLs for durable context and verify subscription after authorized recovery.

options.name: authentication / polling
values: classic PAT notifications/repo scopes per current notification docs
options.decision_rule: Do not assume fine-grained/App tokens support notification endpoints. Respect server polling interval and conditional requests.
options.verification: Inspect authentication compatibility and 304 semantics without exposing credentials; permission failure remains unknown state.

options.name: activity feed window
options.decision_rule: Use feeds for discovery, not real-time completion or complete audit history. Prefer owning issue/PR/commit state for consequential facts.
options.verification: Record event ID/time and owning object evidence; honor ETag and X-Poll-Interval.

pitfalls: Personal inbox Done is unrelated to issue closure or Project Done; never complete work by clearing its notification.

groups.title: Reusable drafts, reversible hiding and temporary interaction limits
groups.applicability: Community repositories with real support/moderation needs; personal replies and broad restrictions require explicit scope.

options.name: saved reply title / body / selection
options.decision_rule: Store generic accurate routing text and customize to the actual report; inserting a draft does not authorize sending. Current documented cap is 100 replies.
options.verification: Reload personal reply settings and preview inserted draft; do not post a test reply.

options.name: minimizeComment.subjectId / classifier
options.decision_rule: Pick a justified classification and preserve the discussion; disagreement or inconvenient findings are not abuse. Check actor/type eligibility first.
options.verification: Read viewerCanMinimize/isMinimized/minimizedReason plus original comment link and rendered visibility.

options.name: unminimize / deletion distinction
options.decision_rule: Use restoration when hiding was mistaken; minimized content still exists and cannot be treated as erased sensitive data.
options.verification: Read restored state and inspect full thread; handle actual secret exposure through the applicable security process.

options.name: interaction scope / inheritance
options.decision_rule: Choose the narrowest incident scope and inspect inherited limits before overriding; broad owner controls affect uninvolved contributors.
options.verification: Read effective repo and owner restrictions and record actor, scope and expiry.

options.name: interaction limit / expiry
options.decision_rule: Prefer the shortest effective restriction consistent with authorized moderation; do not silently block ordinary reporters for routine setup.
options.verification: Read limit and expires_at from owning endpoint and inspect class semantics; never validate by posting disruption.

options.name: remove / expire / blocked users
options.decision_rule: Restore normal participation after incident and keep rationale; removing a repository limit does not remove an inherited owner restriction.
options.verification: Re-read repo/owner limit state and separate block lists where authorized; distinguish expired from inaccessible.

pitfalls: No stable saved-reply CRUD API is established here; inspect current UI. Comment minimization, conversation lock, interaction limit and account blocking are separate controls.

groups.title: Personal availability, bookmarks, featured work and following
groups.applicability: Personal-account actions only when the user requests them; not mandatory repository setup.

options.name: status content / scope
options.decision_rule: Preserve user wording and audience; avoid publishing private project details as status. Organization-scoped status is not an organization announcement.
options.verification: Read emoji/message/organization and inspect rendering as intended audience.

options.name: status availability / expiration
options.decision_rule: Set busy only for requested availability; use intended timezone converted to exact expiry rather than leave a temporary absence indefinitely.
options.verification: Read indicatesLimitedAvailability/expiresAt and verify removal/expiry; personal status is unrelated to work-item Status.

options.name: star list name / description / membership
options.decision_rule: Keep bookmark organization separate from follow/watch; preserve unrelated list memberships in updateUserListsForItem replacement operations.
options.verification: Read list ID/content and repository star state separately; list deletion is not repository deletion.

options.name: profile README / pins
options.decision_rule: Publish only user-approved profile content and intended public featured work; use valid account-named repository for README.
options.verification: Read immutable README commit and public rendered profile/pin order; preserve existing selections.

options.name: contribution/profile visibility
options.decision_rule: Treat as personal privacy choice; anonymized private activity is not permission to reveal private repository names.
options.verification: Inspect profile as owner and public viewer; verify current UI rather than assume profile REST edits cover these settings.

options.name: organization following
options.decision_rule: Follow only requested organizations; preview feature supplies public activity, not membership or repository access.
options.verification: Read following relation as same viewer and inspect dashboard; no requirement to generate activity for a test.

pitfalls: Personal starring, following, availability and profile changes can reveal preferences and should not be silently bundled with a repository audit.

groups.title: Sponsors identity, eligibility and public listing
groups.applicability: Only an owner requesting fundraising; a public/open-source repository does not establish Sponsors eligibility or authorize enrollment.

options.name: listing identity
options.decision_rule: Select the actual beneficiary, authority and supported region/fiscal-host route; do not create an organization listing for a similarly named repository owner by assumption.
options.verification: Read listing/account IDs, owner/admin role and enrollment/approval state.

options.name: profile fields / featured opt-in
options.decision_rule: Prepare accurate public purpose and benefits; owner decides marketing consent and funding language.
options.verification: Read rendered listing and saved preferences; unpublished/draft differs from publicly approved listing.

options.name: onboarding personal/legal fields
options.decision_rule: Let account owner handle required legal/banking attestations and credentials; never infer those from GitHub profile geography or commit email.
options.verification: Report exact outstanding setup gate without exposing tax/bank data; listing mutation alone is not completed onboarding.

options.name: publication / funding link
options.decision_rule: Add funding links only to real intended supported beneficiaries; distinguish external funding URLs from an active GitHub Sponsors listing.
options.verification: Open public listing and repository sponsor target as intended reader; retain owner decision about platform selection.

pitfalls: Enrollment/profile setup does not authorize a payment, bank change, tier publication or newsletter.

groups.title: Amounts, recurrence, publication and benefit access
groups.applicability: Approved Sponsors owner with a concrete benefit/price policy; tier creation is optional.

options.name: amount / recurrence
options.decision_rule: Choose explicitly approved price and monthly versus one-time meaning; never confuse dollars with cents or interpret isRecurring as an arbitrary billing scheduler.
options.verification: Read amount/currency/recurrence from returned tier and actual checkout; current API schema defines valid range.

options.name: description / welcome message
options.decision_rule: Promise only deliverable benefits, avoid private credentials in broad welcome text, and document entitlement expectations.
options.verification: Preview public and purchaser-facing text and check instructions/links.

options.name: publish / retire
options.decision_rule: Review concrete tier before publication. Published prices cannot be edited; retire and create a new tier for a new price.
options.verification: Read published/retired state and remaining active sponsorships; retirement does not cancel existing sponsors.

options.name: repository benefit
options.decision_rule: Adding a benefit grants read-only access to sponsors and requires explicit access authorization; do not attach source or customer data accidentally.
options.verification: Verify exact repository owner/visibility and tier benefit, plus current entitlement policy without creating a paid test sponsorship.

options.name: tier limits
options.decision_rule: Reuse meaningful existing offers rather than create redundant tiers; keep retired options visible in historical reporting.
options.verification: Count active published tiers by recurrence and inspect retired-tier subscribers separately.

pitfalls: Existing sponsors can remain on a retired tier. Do not delete/replace historical tier identity to make the public price list look tidy.

groups.title: Payer intent, bulk partial outcomes and sponsorship privacy
groups.applicability: Only explicit sponsorship instructions naming payer, beneficiary, amount, recurrence and intended visibility.

options.name: sponsorship payer / beneficiary / tier
options.decision_rule: Resolve exact accounts and a current valid offer; do not charge a personal account when organization funding was intended.
options.verification: Read account/tier IDs and current sponsorship before mutation; checkout fees/tax/payment details require current verification.

options.name: one-time / recurring commitment
options.decision_rule: Repository setup and recommendation do not authorize spending. Match the explicitly requested commitment and inspect immediate/prorated effects before submission.
options.verification: Read resulting amount, recurrence, payer, beneficiary and active/pending status; financial mutation timeout requires reconcile-before-retry.

options.name: bulk sponsorship results
options.decision_rule: Treat batch as potentially partial, never all-or-nothing; preserve successful commitments and retry only missing authorized ones.
options.verification: Read every beneficiary relationship and error individually, compare total approved versus committed amounts.

options.name: change / cancel
options.decision_rule: Apply requested effective change with current billing semantics; cancellation does not prove refund or immediate entitlement end.
options.verification: Read resulting tier/state and billing effective date; preserve history of previous commitments.

options.name: privacy / email preferences
options.decision_rule: Make public identity and update consent deliberate personal choices; private sponsorship does not mean beneficiary sees no information.
options.verification: Read actual sponsorship preference fields and public appearance; never publish identity merely to test visibility.

options.name: connected platform
values: Patreon linkage or documented connected sponsorability preference
options.decision_rule: Connect only an explicitly selected owned account and inspect permission scope; linkage does not create a paid sponsorship.
options.verification: Read linkage/preference state and retain external-provider limitations; do not claim payment from a connected badge.

pitfalls: Current billing/provider terms are changeable. Read the actual checkout/account flow before any authorized commitment and keep sensitive financial data out of public issues.

groups.title: Sponsor history, exports and referral metadata
groups.applicability: Sponsors owners requesting financial/activity reporting; exports contain personal/financial information.
